data.content_ref: inline:The interventionist criterion in SRC_003 and SRC_001 reduces to a special case of the epistemological frame dependence described in SRC_002 and SRC_004: an intervention on a postulated shared cause only yields evidence of dependence relative to the analyst's current model and accessible variables, so successful manipulation never establishes an ontological fact of dependence but merely revises the epistemic boundary between 'uncorrelated' and 'independent'. It is refuted if one can exhibit an intervention whose outcome is invariant across all epistemic frames and model expansions (i.e., an intervention that settles ontological dependence independently of the observer's background knowledge).
